newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's US$3.4 bln chemical complex restarted.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's US$3.4 bln chemical complex restarted.

text.p: Singapore's new US$3.4 billion petrochemical complex is back on stream after teething start up problems forced a shutdown on April 28, nine days after it began operations, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
"Our plants re-started last week and are currently in operation," Petrochemical Corporation of Singapore (PCS) said in a written reply to a Reuters' query.
PCS owns the core 515,000 tonne per year ethylene plant which provides feedstock to several derivative plants, including those for the production of polyethylene, polypropylene and styrene monomer.
The products are used to make a variety of plastic products for both domestic and industrial use.
The company is a 50:50 joint venture between Royal Dutch Shell and a Sumitomo Chemical led consortium of Japanese companies firms also owns Singapore's first ethylene plant.

One of the bigger downstream plant in the complex that has also started up is The Polyolefin Co's (TPC) polyethylene and polypropylene plant with annual capacities 190,000 tonnes and 120,000 tonnes, respectively.
But another large plant, a 450,000 tonne per year styrene monomer/propylene oxide, is facing start up problems of its own, industry sources said.
The plant, 70-percent owned by Shell, is expected to start up later this week, industry sources said. The company failed to to start up last week, the sources said.
"Downstream plants have restarted or are in the process of starting up their plants," PCS said in reply to a query on the status of the two derivative plants.
Industry sources said that even after the two plants begin operations, PCS is not expected to operate at full capacity until the third quarter due to the late start up of a third big downstream unit.

The 200,000 tonne per year polyethylene plant is expected to begin operations in July, industry sources said. The plant is 50-percent owned by Phillips Petroleum with the remaining share taken up by the Singapore government and Sumitomo Chemical.
PCS also said that the complex will be shutdown next year for scheduled maintenance works.
